title: Tiered rollout controller for deterministic GPU-slice upgrades
creator: Diego Alvarez
description:
Problem: Upgrading dedicated GPU pools today is brittle: drains cause transient capacity shortfalls, autoscalers fight eviction, and tenants see spike in request queue times. We need a controller that executes deterministic, tenant-aware upgrades in slices (sub-pools of GPUs) while coordinating with the autoscaler and rollout gates tied to LTS channel semantics.

Goal: Implement a Tiered Rollout Controller (TRC) that: 1) splits a pool into upgrade slices based on tenant affinity and device topology, 2) negotiates an explicit autoscaler handshake to lock an eviction budget for each slice, 3) enforces rollout gates (SLA, error budget, warmup checks) before progressing, and 4) exposes observability and manual override hooks to the Console. The controller should default to conservative settings for LTS channels and allow faster pacing for edge releases.

Success criteria: (a) no more than 2% SLA drift on p99 latency measured per-tenant during any upgrade wave, (b) <1.5x spike in queue time for affected requests, (c) zero silent failures during slice handoff (errors surfaced to Console and rollback initiated), and (d) runbook steps validated in a staged canary with synthetic traffic.
comments: 2026-03-01 Diego Alvarez: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/TRC+Design. Decided to target slices by tenant affinity + physical rack to reduce cross-rack evictions.

2026-03-03 Marta Chen: Proposal added: use 'eviction-token' handshake with autoscaler API v2. Autoscaler must respond with a guaranteed capacity window before we initiate drain (PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-autoscaler/pull/487).

2026-03-05 Stef Nguyen (SRE): Concern: conservative token sizes will waste utilization. Suggest proportional token sizing based on historical tail utilization per-tenant. Added as deferred optimization.

2026-03-07 Ravi Patel (PM): Rollout gate list approved: (1) preflight health check (image & kernel match), (2) p50/p95 latency baseline within 5% of baseline, (3) error rate < 0.1% over 5m. If a gate fails, controller should pause and alert.
2026-03-09 Security review (LZ): No KMS changes required. Ensure audit events emitted for token grants and slice completion (tracked in runtime-1.19 security checklist).

2026-03-11 Design feedback (Anna Li): Console needs a ‘slice timeline’ visualization with predicted completion times and active token owners. Mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/design/trc-slice-timeline.png
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial design doc completed. Chose three-tier slice sizing: small (1-2 GPUs), medium (3-6), large (7+). Decision rationale: small slices for high-tenancy churn, medium for general use, large for single-tenant high-throughput pools.
2026-03-04: Implemented basic slice allocator prototype (internal branch: feature/trc-slice-allocator). Unit tests for affinity grouping added. Basic acceptance tests run in staging cluster.

2026-03-06: Autoscaler handshake API defined (autoscaler v2): grantEvictionToken(pool, slice_id, desired_capacity, ttl) -> {token, guaranteed_capacity}. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/487. Waiting on infra review.

2026-03-08: Added rollout gate evaluator that consumes metrics from the Console metrics API. Metrics required: per-tenant latency percentiles, node allocation success ratio, request queue length. Implemented simulated gate runs against historical traces to validate thresholds.

2026-03-11: Staged canary run scheduled for 2026-03-18 on pool gpu-ord-2 with synthetic traffic. Canary will exercise small -> medium slice path and validate rollback behavior on injected error scenarios.
2026-03-12: Manual control endpoints added to controller API: pause(slice_id), resume(slice_id), abort(slice_id). Auth integration wired to RBAC team role 'release-operator'.

tradeoffs_and_open_questions: Reserving guaranteed capacity reduces overall cluster utilization – trade-off between predictable SLOs and cost. We decided conservative defaults for LTS, with a config toggle for fast channels.
How large should eviction tokens be for mixed-tenant pools? Current plan uses historical 95th percentile per-tenant; still need validation for new tenants with no history.
Fallback behavior: immediate rollback vs staged ramp-down. Current approach: staged rollback (re-insert drained nodes with higher eviction backoff) to avoid cascading autoscaler reactions.
Long-running in-flight requests: whether to rely on preemption or graceful drain only. We prefer graceful drain with max_kill_timeout but will add a preemption hook for emergency aborts.

notes: Related reading: design notes from ENG-27109 (adaptive-drain-scheduler) influenced the handshake model.
We should avoid coupling TRC progress to global autoscaler decisions; handshake makes progress idempotent and scoped to pool/slice.
Console UX must surface both predicted and observed completion times — projection algorithm baked into allocator service.
If canary shows >2% p99 drift we will abort and pivot to increased reservation sizes for LTS channels.
